decisions.statement: premerge-check reads the review report and finding files from the branch head with git and reruns the gates in the story's checkout; this rule was added to the story workflow proposal.
decisions.quote: I added the rule to the "Checks at the merge" section, along with one completion criterion for it.

decisions.statement: The lector's cut plan for story-workflow.md is applied as approved (order and duplicate changes), without the proposed empty Appendix.
decisions.quote: The lector agent is now applying the approved cuts and will do the sentence pass afterwards.

decisions.statement: The handback completion criterion names the output of premerge-check rather than the output of each gate.
decisions.quote: The handback criterion now names "the output of `premerge-check`".

decisions.statement: The story workflow is treated as a subset of the dispatch process; work goes upstream to define the whole dispatch process first.
decisions.quote: Story workflow is a subset of the dispatch process. Let's go upstream.

decisions.statement: A run driven by hand has the same frame as an orchestrated run: feature branch, ledger, story branches cut from the feature branch, and an end.
decisions.quote: Settled: both ways share one frame.

decisions.statement: The person who drives a run by hand gets thorough guidance, which becomes its own part of the proposal.
decisions.quote: The person who drives by hand gets thorough guidance, which will become its own part of the proposal.

decisions.statement: The human merges the feature branch into dev on both ways, after the check command passes.
decisions.quote: Settled: the human merges into `dev` on both ways, after the check command passes.

decisions.statement: dispatch close removes all state of the run and keeps no record beyond git history and the story files.
decisions.quote: Settled: `dispatch close` removes everything of the run and keeps no record beyond git history and the story files.

decisions.statement: A run ends either finished or dropped; afterwards only unmerged branches remain, and the human deletes them.
decisions.quote: Settled: a run ends either finished or dropped. In both cases nothing of the run remains except unmerged branches, and the human deletes those.

decisions.statement: One run may be active per feature branch; every check whether a run is active reads only the ledger of its own branch.
decisions.quote: Settled: one run per feature branch. Every check that asks whether a run is active reads only the ledger of its own branch.

decisions.statement: The merge sets a story to done on both ways, and the human driving by hand merges with dispatch merge-story.
decisions.quote: Settled: the merge sets `done` on both ways, and the human who drives by hand merges with `dispatch merge-story`.

decisions.statement: The number of fix rounds is configurable, with three rounds on the story's tier plus three with a stronger model as the default.
decisions.quote: Can we make the count configurable and use these 3+3 as default?

decisions.statement: When tests fail after a story merge, the feature branch moves back to the commit before the merge, and the spec changes to match the code.
decisions.quote: Settled: the feature branch moves back to the commit before the failed merge, and the spec changes to match the code.

decisions.statement: The next wave starts only after the previous wave is closed; by hand each story is a wave of its own.
decisions.quote: Settled: the next wave starts only after the previous wave is closed, and by hand each story is a wave of its own.

decisions.statement: The implementation agent runs the gates on both ways, and the developer agent never runs a gate script.
decisions.quote: Settled: the implementation agent runs the gates on both ways, and the developer agent never runs a gate script.

decisions.statement: Where a document and the code disagree with no design question behind it, the document changes to match the code.
decisions.quote: Recorded: where a document and the code disagree with no design question behind it, the document changes to match the code.

decisions.statement: Development, tests, code review, CRAP, mutation testing and QA with their fix loops belong inside the run; reconciliation runs on dev after the merge.
decisions.quote: Recorded: development, tests, code review, CRAP, mutation testing and QA, each with its fix loop, belong inside the run. Reconciliation runs on `dev` after the merge.

decisions.statement: Per-story steps (TDD, tests, story code review, crap-score, mutation testing) run on the story branch; the end-of-feature code review stays and runs with QA on the feature branch; a security scan is added per story.
decisions.quote: Recorded: the split as I described it, with the code review at the end of the feature kept, and a security scan added per story.

decisions.statement: Security scanning per story is a deterministic scanner gate, configurable per project: each project chooses whether to enable it and which scanners to run.
decisions.quote: Recorded: a deterministic scanner gate per story, configured per project. Each project chooses whether to enable it and which scanners to run.

decisions.statement: Drift sessions for spec-feedback rows run at the close of each wave, not after each merge.
decisions.quote: I take "BZ" as B: the drift sessions run at the close of each wave.

decisions.statement: Every ledger field must have a command that reads it; fields without a reader (gate_results, closed) are dropped.
decisions.quote: It also gives the ledger's mode field a reader, so it passes the ledger rule you just accepted.

decisions.statement: The ledger field commit_sha keeps holding the merge commit after a merge; no separate field for the story's own commit.
decisions.quote: No command needs the story's own commit after the merge, so the field can stay as it is.

decisions.statement: The ledger records how the run is driven, with mode values orchestrated and by-hand.
decisions.quote: Settled: the ledger records the mode

decisions.statement: Every enforcement mechanism must work in all supported agent CLIs, or it is designed differently.
decisions.quote: This must either work for all CLIs or we must design it differently.

decisions.statement: In a run driven by hand, the git guardrail refuses agents the commands that need a person, and the human runs them; OpenCode gets the git guardrail as part of this work.
decisions.quote: Settled: in a run driven by hand, the git guardrail refuses agents the commands that need a person, and you run those commands yourself. OpenCode gets the git guardrail as part of this work.

decisions.statement: At each by-hand stop the agent shows the premerge-check output, the findings with their status and the branch head, and gives the exact command to run.
decisions.quote: Each stop shows the `premerge-check` output, the findings with their status and the branch head, and it gives the exact command to run.

decisions.statement: The proposal uses one vocabulary: run, orchestrated, by hand, feature branch, story branch, gate-check step, spawn, spec-feedback report, primary checkout; dispatch names only the script.
decisions.quote: Settled: the proposal uses only that vocabulary.

decisions.statement: dispatch close also closes old leftover runs, and dispatch close --orphans lists worktrees and branches without a ledger.
decisions.quote: Settled: `dispatch close` also closes the old runs, and `--orphans` lists what has no ledger.

decisions.statement: One new proposal, docs/proposals/run-lifecycle.md, covers the run lifecycle and supersedes story-workflow.md.
decisions.quote: `story-workflow.md` is marked `superseded`, and a line at its top points to the new proposal.
